metadata.difficultyReason: Forty questions across nine paper pages use a separate image sheet, multi-part calculations and explanations, and a 78-point published rubric.
topics: active and passive sensing, radar altimetry and satellite instruments
satellite orbits and spatial, temporal, radiometric and spectral resolution
Sentinel-2 false-color imagery, NDVI, NDWI, and land-cover classification
metadata.alignment: Most topics overlap the 2027 Division B Remote Sensing rules, including satellite imagery, atmospheric effects, resolution, and vegetation/water indices. The paper's quantitative Snell's-law refraction item exceeds the 2027 B rules' starred-equation scope, so this is marked as a different-topic practice test.
metadata.scoringBasis: The test cover states 78 points. Questions 1–40 have printed point values in the paper/key; the 0-point dynamic CO2 tiebreaker is excluded. The 40 scores sum to 78.
metadata.instructions: Use the complete original paper and any supplements. Answer all labeled parts.

fields.prompt: The blue color of the sky is primarily derived from what type of scattering? What conditions are required for this type of scattering to occur? (2)
fields.answer: Rayleigh scattering, when the particle size is much smaller than the wavelength of the light

criteria.answer: particle size much smaller than wavelength
accepted: particle size is much smaller than the wavelength of the light
particle size much smaller than wavelength

fields.prompt:
Identify the most appropriate method of imaging for each of the following scenarios, choosing from: I) Active sensing II) Whisk broom passive sensing III) Push broom passive sensing; each term may be used multiple times or none at all. (4)

_____ An aircraft is rapidly flying over a field and wants to image the vegetation underneath.
_____ A satellite in geostationary orbit wants to vertically profile clouds in order to predict rainfall.
_____ Bob wants to build his own remote sensor. He is financially limited but wants a flexible sensor that can scan various specialized geometry or terrains.
_____ Alice also wants a remote sensor, but she wants whichever option that can provide the highest resolution.
fields.answer: III, I, II, I

fields.prompt: What are two ways that remote sensing can be used in forecasting volcanic eruptions? (2)
fields.answer: Any two distinct methods: detect ground deformation using altimetry/radar; measure surface temperature with a radiometer/pyrometer/thermometer; or measure gas emission/content with a spectrometer. For each method, award 0.5 for the observation and 0.5 for an appropriate instrument.

criteria.answer: First valid observation: ground deformation, surface temperature change, or gas emissions/content
Matching instrument for first observation: radar/altimetry, radiometer/pyrometer/thermometer, or spectrometer
Second distinct valid observation from the published key

fields.prompt: A beam of light enters from air (index of refraction = 1.0) to a layer of peculiar air with index of refraction of 1.25 at an angle of 60º from the normal. At what angle from the normal would the light beam emerge from the peculiar air back into air, if at all? Show your work or reasoning. (3)
fields.answer: The angle is still 60º, because the initial and final media have the same indices of refraction.

criteria.answer: Because the incident and final media are both air with the same refractive index, the exiting angle equals 60 degrees; accept equivalent Snell's-law work.
accepted: initial and final media have the same indices of refraction

fields.prompt: What units are the margins of the map labeled with? (1)
fields.answer: Degrees, arcminutes or minutes of arc or minutes

fields.prompt: What remote sensing technique is primarily used to obtain this image? Briefly explain how this technique is able to measure the elevation of the ground. (3)
fields.answer: Radar altimetry, it sends pulses towards the ground and measures the time it takes the pulse to bounce off the ground back to the sensor.

accepted: measures the time it takes the pulse to bounce off the ground back to the sensor

fields.prompt: What region of the electromagnetic spectrum does this technique primarily operate in? (1)
fields.answer: Microwave

fields.prompt: Name something else that this technique could be good for measuring. (1)
fields.answer: Any reasonable radar/radar-altimeter use, including cloud or precipitation profiling, probing under ground or ice, or anti-aircraft radar applications.

fields.prompt: What is the overall trend of this region’s change in elevation?
fields.answer: b

fields.prompt: What is a likely anthropogenic cause for the change you selected in the previous question? Briefly explain the mechanism through which it occurs. (3)
fields.answer: Groundwater extraction faster than the rate of replenishment, causing aquifer pores to empty and collapse, lowering surface elevation.

accepted: Groundwater extraction faster than the rate of replenishment
causing aquifer pores to empty and collapse
lowering surface elevation due to aquifer collapse

fields.prompt: List two natural and two anthropogenic sources of aerosols on Earth. (2)
fields.answer: Natural: volcanic eruptions, forest fires. Anthropogenic: burning fossil fuels, refrigerants.

accepted: wind blowing dust into the air
wind blowing dust into the air

fields.prompt:
Refer to Image 2, which depicts aerosol hotspots across the globe during January and July. Match the months to each image and give one reason of how you can tell. (2)

2a: __________
2b: __________
fields.answer: 2a: July, 2b: January, with reasoning about monsoon or ITCZ position.

accepted: more human activity or plant emissions during summer
more fires tend to occur during summer
data range covers more of northern hemisphere in 2a

fields.prompt: What instrument on Terra took these images? How does it physically measure aerosol concentration? (2)
fields.answer: MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer), it measures aerosol optical depth computed from spectral analysis of reflected sunlight.

accepted: computed from spectral analysis reflected sunlight

fields.prompt: Explain the Twomey effect. Be sure to explain how the addition of aerosols influences clouds and ultimately Earth’s radiative balance. (3)
fields.answer: Aerosols lead to smaller droplet sizes as condensation nuclei, causing clouds to reflect more sunlight and cool the Earth.

fields.prompt: Explain how the opposite of what you described above might be true (e.g. if you previously concluded the Twomey effect states aerosols cool the Earth, now propose a process by which aerosols can warm the Earth, and vice versa). (2)
fields.answer: Dark aerosols such as dust or soot absorb heat and reradiate it to heat up the surrounding atmosphere.

accepted: Dark aerosols such as dust or soot
absorb heat and reradiate it to heat up the surrounding atmosphere

fields.prompt: How is false color implemented in the context of remote sensing (as opposed to true color)? Which image(s) between 3a-c display(s) false coloration, if any? (3)
fields.answer: Colors assigned are not what they directly appear as in real life, especially for non-optical radiation such as infrared. Images 3b and 3c.

accepted: Colors assigned to the image are not what they directly appear as in real life
non-optical radiation mapped to visible colors

fields.prompt: What orbit is Sentinel-2 in and why might that be helpful for its task? (2)
fields.answer: Sun-synchronous, passes over the same region at the same local solar time to ensure consistent lighting conditions for comparison.

accepted: passes over the same region at the same local solar time

fields.prompt: Sentinel-2 has a spatial resolution of 10 meters in Image 3a. A square of what area is covered by each pixel? Assuming the images provided are 32.5 km by 53 km, what is overall resolution of Image 3a? Show your work. (4)
fields.answer: 100 m^2 per pixel; 3250 pixels x 5300 pixels (or 17,225,000 pixels)

fields.prompt:
Match the following descriptions of Sentinel-2 to the type of resolution being described, choosing from: Temporal, Radiometric, Spectral. (3)

___________ Sentinel-2’s 12-bit resolution allows it to distinguish between 4,096 levels of brightness
___________ Sentinel-2 has 13 bands, covering the electromagnetic spectrum from 442 nm to 2202.4 nm
___________ Sentinel-2 revisits the same location every 5 days
fields.answer: Radiometric, Spectral, Temporal

fields.prompt: What general region of the electromagnetic spectrum is used to produce Image 3a? (1)
fields.answer: Visible

fields.prompt: Are the clouds displayed near the top right of Image 3a high or low clouds? Do you expect them to contribute to a net warming or cooling of the surface? Explain. (3)
fields.answer: High clouds, net warming because they are thin and reflect light poorly but absorb and reradiate outgoing longwave radiation.

criteria.answer: Thin high clouds reflect incoming sunlight poorly
They absorb and reradiate outgoing longwave radiation

fields.prompt: In Image 3a, what color generally corresponds to the densest vegetation?
fields.answer: e

fields.prompt: In Image 3b, what color generally corresponds to the densest vegetation?
fields.answer: e

fields.prompt: In Image 3c, what generally color corresponds to the densest vegetation?
fields.answer: a

fields.prompt: Which of the labeled points on the surface has the highest albedo?
fields.answer: d

fields.prompt:
Place the following electromagnetic regions on the spectrum provided: near infrared (NIR), far infrared (FIR), short-wave infrared (SWIR), mid-wave infrared (MWIR), long-wave infrared (LWIR). (2)

Visible _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ Microwave
fields.answer: NIR, SWIR, MWIR, LWIR, FIR

criteria.answer: Order from visible toward microwave: NIR, SWIR, MWIR, LWIR, FIR; start from 2 points and subtract 0.5 for each wrong placement.
accepted: Near Infrared, Short-wave infrared, Mid-wave infrared, Long-wave infrared, Far infrared

fields.prompt: Image 3b utilizes the NDVI to display vegetation health. What does NDVI stand for? (1)
fields.answer: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index

fields.prompt: The NDVI calculation requires the visible red and what region of the infrared spectrum as listed in the previous question? What bands do they correspond to, respectively? (2)
fields.answer: NIR; red = B04, NIR = B08

criteria.answer: Visible red is Sentinel-2 band B04

fields.prompt: The data utilized in NDVI primarily relies on which of the following interactions of light with vegetation?
fields.answer: a

fields.prompt:
Image 3c utilizes the NDWI, a similar index for water instead of vegetation. It can be calculated using the following formula for Sentinel-2: NDWI = (Band 3 - Band 8) / (Band 3 + Band 8). Circle the words that best complete the following sentence: (2)

If Band 3 receives a much stronger signal than Band 8, the NDWI will be (low/high), indicating (water/dry land). Band 8 is (longer/shorter) in wavelength than Band 3, as water produces stronger signal in (longer/shorter) wavelengths compared to dry land.
fields.answer: high, water, longer, shorter

criteria.answer: Band 8 has a longer wavelength than Band 3
Water produces a stronger signal at shorter wavelengths than dry land

fields.prompt: What is the range of all possible values for the NDWI? In other words, what are the lowest and highest possible NDWI values? (1)
fields.answer: -1 to 1

fields.prompt: What color in image 3c has the lowest NDWI value? (1)
fields.answer: White

fields.prompt: Which of the following best identifies the features circled in E on the maps?
fields.answer: d

fields.prompt: Use evidence from at least 2 images between 3a-c to support your choice above. (2)
fields.answer: Award 1 point each for two valid observations from different images 3a–3c that support the chosen answer to question 33. For artificial ponds: 3a dark/low albedo; 3b red like the bay/low vegetation or NDVI; 3c blue like other water bodies/high NDWI. The published key also accepts evidence appropriate to a different choice in question 33.

criteria.answer: First relevant observation from one of images 3a–3c supporting the student's question 33 choice
Second relevant observation from a different image among 3a–3c

fields.prompt: Other than point B, which labeled point/region would you expect to have the highest risk of flooding (choose from A, C, D, E)? Briefly explain your answer. (2)
fields.answer: Point C, located at a low elevation (likely a wetland) and very close to water bodies.

fields.prompt: At which labeled point would you expect to have the lowest variation in daily temperature? Why? (2)
fields.answer: Point B, as water has high heat capacity and acts as a buffer for temperature changes.

accepted: acts as a buffer for temperature changes

fields.prompt: Notice the main river on the left. Which general direction is it flowing in?
fields.answer: c

fields.prompt: Notice that the majority of the branches of the river are to the west side of the river. Why might that be the case? (2)
fields.answer: Elevation increases relatively steeply (there is a hill) to the east and prevents meandering channels, unlike the flatter west.

accepted: elevation increases relatively steeply to the east
there is a hill to the east
unlike the west that is relatively flat

fields.prompt:
Refer to image Image 4d, which shows the annual NLCD land classification by the USGS in 2024. Assign a Land Cover Class, as below, to each labeled point in Image 4d. (4)

a. Developed ____ Point W
b. Barren ____ Point X
c. Herbaceous ____ Point Y
d. Shrubland ____ Point Z
e. Cultivated
f. Wetland
fields.answer: Point W: f, Point X: c, Point Y: e, Point Z: a
fields.context: The original question says images 4d/4e, but the supplied image sheet labels the corresponding land-cover maps 3d (2024) and 3e (2004). Use those maps.

fields.prompt: Compare Image 4d with 4e, which is the NLCD classification for 2004. What are two differences that you notice? (2)
fields.answer: Valid observations such as part of the wetland becoming cultivated or urbanization in the northeast corner.

accepted: Part of the wetland has become cultivated
drying of some permanently flooded areas to become wetlands
areas of water body becoming barren

criteria.answer: A second distinct, relevant land-cover change between the 2004 and 2024 maps
accepted: Part of the wetland has become cultivated
drying of some permanently flooded areas to become wetlands
areas of water body becoming barren

fields.context: The original question says images 4d/4e, but the supplied image sheet labels the corresponding land-cover maps 3d (2024) and 3e (2004). Use those maps.
